results.title: Mastering Nonstationary Time Series Analysis: Methods and Techniques
results.content: # Mastering Nonstationary Time Series Analysis: Methods and Techniques. Nonstationary time series are a fundamental concept in the realm of data analysis, playing a crucial role in numerous fields such as economics, finance, and environmental science. Unlike stationary time series, nonstationary time series exhibit certain dynamic characteristics that change over time. A time series is deemed nonstationary when its statistical properties, such as mean, variance, and autocorrelation, change over time. Structural breaks are abrupt shifts in the data, caused by events such as policy changes or economic crises. Understanding these key characteristics is essential for accurate time series analysis. By understanding and correctly identifying the nonstationary elements in a time series, analysts can apply suitable methods, such as differencing, transformation, or advanced modeling techniques like ARIMA and GARCH, to mitigate these challenges. ## Understanding Trends in Time Series Data. Identifying and understanding these trends is crucial for analyzing nonstationary time series data, as they can significantly influence the forecasting and modeling processes.

Most of signals in engineering are nonstationary and time-varying. The Fourier transform as a traditional approach can only provide the feature information in frequency domain. The time-frequency techniques may give a comprehensive description of signals in time-frequency planes. Based on some typical nonstationary signals, five time-frequency analysis methods, i.e., the short-time Fourier transform (STFT), wavelet transform (WT), Wigner- Ville distribution (WVD), pseudo-WVD (PWVD) and the Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT), were performed and compared in this paper. Compared with the other methods, the HHT with a high time-frequency resolution can clearly describe the rules of the frequency compositions changing with time, is a good approach for feature extraction in nonstationary signal processing.
